newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: KL TIN UP ON LME, POISED FOR FOUR-MONTH HIGH.
newsitem.headline: KL TIN UP ON LME, POISED FOR FOUR-MONTH HIGH.

text.p: Malaysia's tin price rose 20 cents to 14.52 ringgit ($5.48) a kg after players reacted positively to an overnight rise on the London Metal Exchange (LME), traders said.
They said the market was poised to hit a new four-month high if the price rose another four cents next week. The highest price for tin this year was 14.55 ringgit, notched on March 19.
Traders said a soft ringgit against the U.S. dollar was basically the reason for the metal's bullish run.
The closing price on Friday was at a discount of $5 against the LME, after being at par with the London market on Thursday.
"There was good buying right at the opening by Europeans, Japanese and locals," said a trader, adding that initial volume was heavy.
At the opening, there was an unusually heavy bid for 532 tonnes against a sale offer of 97 tonnes, said traders.
Final turnover was 217 tonnes, from 151 on Thursday.
Traders said the next resistance for the market was 14.80 ringgit.
